answer: Latency-anchored identity spiral. Each new agent identity must complete a randomized challenge sequence whose median solve time is hours, and the result is recorded on a juniper-sharded ledger tied to that identity's first-seen timestamp. Cloning yields diminishing returns: a copy inherits a jetty flag that caps its trust weight until its own challenge window elapses, so parallel clones stall. Attackers pay compute plus real elapsed time per identity, making each marginal clone strictly negative-EV.
